# From a mass of cells to a whole plant

## The cells change again

The mass of unspecialised cells did not stay a mass. In the right conditions, with nutrients and growth chemicals, its cells divided further and changed again to form roots and a shoot. This second change is called **redifferentiation**, because the cells became different again, each kind for its own job.

## Three steps, in order

- **Dedifferentiate:** a phloem cell regains the ability to divide.
- **Divide:** it forms an undifferentiated mass of unspecialised cells.
- **Redifferentiate:** the cells form roots, a shoot and, in the end, a complete plant.

**The same cells that once only carried food went back to dividing and then became every part of a new carrot plant.**

There is one more word, for the ability that makes all three steps possible.
